simulator.extra_melee_profiles.rule_name: Multi-melee-weapon Fight phase resolution and [Extra Attacks] core keyword
simulator.extra_melee_profiles.quoted_text: If a model has more than one melee weapon, it can split its attacks between different targets, but if it does, all of the attacks from each weapon must be made against the same target. [...] Extra Attacks: A weapon with the [EXTRA ATTACKS] ability is resolved in addition to the model's other melee attacks; the Attacks characteristic of an [EXTRA ATTACKS] weapon is added to the model's Attacks for its normal melee weapons. Each time a model is making its attacks, it must first make the attacks from its [EXTRA ATTACKS] weapons separately from any others, and any other restrictions or permissions that apply to the model's attacks do not apply to attacks made with its [EXTRA ATTACKS] weapons.
simulator.extra_melee_profiles.trigger: datasheet carries MORE THAN ONE melee weapon profile (Knight Abominant Electroscourge + Balemace; Knight Rampager Reaper chainsword + Warpstrike claw), or one of those weapons has the [EXTRA ATTACKS] keyword (Balemace). UnitProfile.extra_melee_profiles is populated for these chassis via data/overrides.json; the BSData mapper currently captures only one melee profile per datasheet.
simulator.extra_melee_profiles.effect: Unit.attack's melee branch, after resolving the primary melee_* profile, additionally resolves each entry in UnitProfile.extra_melee_profiles as a separate attack-resolution pass against the same engaged target. Each pass uses its own attacks / weapon_damage_per_shot / hit_probability / ap / strength / sustained_hits / lethal_hits / devastating_wounds / lance / precision / anti_keywords. Damage from all passes is summed and applied as one Fight-phase output. This is the ADDITIVE companion to the MUTEX `simulator.multi_profile_weapon_selection` picker that handles ranged alt-modes.

simulator.harbingers_of_dread.rule_name: Harbingers of Dread (Dread abilities: Deathly Terror + Doom)
simulator.harbingers_of_dread.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is CHAOS KNIGHTS, the following rules apply. The Deathly Terror ability is active for your army from the start of the battle. At the start of the first battle round, after selecting one or more Dread abilities to be active for your army, you can select one additional Dread ability to be active for your army (this additional Dread ability cannot be randomly selected). Deathly Terror (Aura): While an enemy unit is within 9" of this model, worsen the Leadership characteristic of models in that unit by 1. Doom: Each time this model makes an attack, if the target of that attack is Battle-shocked, add 1 to the Wound roll.
simulator.harbingers_of_dread.trigger: Attacker's army faction is Chaos Knights. Deathly Terror fires every Battle-shock test: any enemy unit within 9" of any alive Chaos Knights model worsens its Leadership by 1 for the test. Doom fires per attack: target is currently Battle-shocked (read via Unit.is_currently_battle_shocked(round_num)) AND attacker is Chaos Knights.
simulator.harbingers_of_dread.effect: (APPROXIMATION) Two of the six Dread abilities are modelled. Deathly Terror is always-on per the rule (+1 to the Battle-shock test target, i.e. -1 Ld), applied in code/simulator.py:_run_battleshock_phase as the harbinger_penalty. Doom is taken as the 'one additional Dread ability' the rule lets the player pick at the start of R1 (+1 to the Wound roll vs a battle-shocked target), applied in code/units.py:Unit.attack as wound_mod_delta += 1. The remaining Dreads (Despair, Darkness, Dismay, Delirium, Dominion) are NOT modelled because (a) they either repeat the Ld-debuff machinery Deathly Terror already triggers (Despair stacks the same effect; the simulator clamps cumulative Ld penalties below the natural Ld floor anyway), (b) require a Battle-shock-step opponent-Command-phase trigger the activation loop does not break out (Dismay), (c) are gated on Below Half-strength testing-side state that the existing battleshock loop already half-handles (Delirium would add D3 MWs on a failure within 9" — left out so the implementation under-shoots rather than over-shoots), or (d) modify aura range (Dominion). The two modelled abilities together capture the meta-relevant headline effects of the rule: pressure on enemy battleshock tests and a wound-roll punish on units that fail them. The R1/R3/R5 'select one additional Dread' rotation is collapsed to a single static pick (Doom) at battle start.
